title: YODA · Data pipelines
description: Airflow's view of the medallion pipeline. Databricks job outcomes are NOT here — they arrive as Azure resource logs in Log Analytics, which Prometheus cannot see. That split is by signal origin, not preference; see docs/OBSERVABILITY.md.

options.content: **Scope.** Orchestration signals only — whether work was scheduled, queued and dispatched. Whether a Databricks job *succeeded*, and whether `gold` is fresh, are Azure resource logs: query `DatabricksJobs` and `DatabricksUnityCatalog` in Log Analytics, or see the `alert-dbx-job-failure` rule. Airflow knows it submitted a run; it does not know the table is correct.

panels.title: Import errors
panels.description: Non-zero means a DAG file is broken and simply absent from the UI. `make dag-test` catches this before merge.

panels.title: Tasks queued
panels.description: Sustained non-zero on this node means the two-concurrent-task ceiling is binding. Deferrable operators are what keep it from being hit — see ADR-014.

panels.title: DAG run schedule delay
panels.description: Gap between when a run was due and when it started. Growth here means the scheduler is behind — the pipeline is late before any task has run.

panels.title: DAG parse duration — logistics_medallion
panels.description: Parse time for the one DAG. A DAG that does work at import time — a query, an API call — shows up here and slows every scheduler loop.

panels.title: Scheduler liveness
panels.description: Heartbeat rate. A flat zero here explains any 'nothing is running' report instantly, and is the first thing to check.

panels.title: Task pod lifecycle
panels.description: KubernetesExecutor creates a pod per task. Pods appearing and completing is the pipeline working; pods appearing and staying Pending is the capacity ceiling.
